headline: Google introduces Gemini 3.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash for agentic AI applications
summary: The new multimodal models offer high speed, cost-efficiency, and a 1 million token input window, making advanced AI development more accessible.
details: Google has launched Gemini 3.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash, its latest AI models designed to power agentic applications. These models aim to meet developers' needs for fast and cost-effective solutions for complex reasoning tasks, combining frontier intelligence with high operational speed.

The Gemini 3.5 series serves as Google's core intelligence layer for 2026, featuring multimodal capabilities by default. It can process and build code across text, audio, video, and PDF formats simultaneously, eliminating the need for external conversion tools.

Specifically engineered for autonomous agents, the API provides low latency and high reliability for tool-calling operations. This makes it a robust platform for agents that need to interact with external tools and make decisions over extended periods.
Gemini 3.5 also excels in code correctness and handles complex system integration tasks with ease. This makes it a strong choice for businesses looking to automate their software delivery lifecycles.

The standout release, Gemini 3.5 Flash, launched in mid-May 2026, prioritizes speed and cost-efficiency. Despite its smaller size, it supports a massive one million token input window, allowing developers to upload entire project codebases or hours of video directly into prompts for quick processing.

Google has also reduced the pricing for the Flash model, making high-volume agentic tasks more affordable for startups and SMEs. This move significantly lowers the barrier to entry for agentic programming.

Developers are leveraging Gemini 3.5 for automated code reviews and refactoring, using its large context window to analyze multiple files for security vulnerabilities and style guide compliance. Another key use case is video and audio analysis, extracting data, summarizing content, and generating code snippets from multimedia.

To further optimize costs and latency, Google introduced context caching for the Gemini 3.5 series. This feature allows developers to store frequently used files in Google's cache, reducing active token processing and cutting running costs by up to 50%.

This caching enables continuous integration scripts to run efficiently, checking every GitHub commit for logical errors without exceeding budgets. Developers can experiment with these features immediately using Google AI Studio, a browser-based playground for testing prompts and API endpoints.

headline_marked: [[Students prefer Gemini over ChatGPT and Claude]] for AI essays in blind tests, StudyArena finds
headline: Students prefer Gemini over ChatGPT and Claude for AI essays in blind tests, StudyArena finds
summary: A StudyArena analysis of 6,851 blind student votes revealed Gemini as the top choice for essay writing, outperforming Claude and ChatGPT with a 39.6% preference rate.
details: StudyArena conducted a blind test with 6,851 student votes across major AI models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. Students chose their preferred response for writing and essay tasks without knowing which model generated it.
Gemini emerged as the top choice for college essay help, securing a 39.6% preference rate. Claude followed with 31.8%, while ChatGPT and other OpenAI models collectively received 29.2% of the votes.
The study suggests Gemini's balance in writing style, avoiding extremes, contributed to its lead. Responses that were complete, structured, and clear without sounding mechanical were favored.
Students also tended to prefer longer responses, with selected answers being 37% longer on average. Higher-effort settings on models did not correlate with higher choice rates for essay prose.
While Gemini leads for overall college writing, each provider has a specialty. Google's Gemini excels in refining existing drafts, leading writing feedback at 41.7%.

Anthropic's Claude family is preferred for assignment planning (43.2%), useful for exploring competing structures before drafting. OpenAI's GPT family leads for research work (39.3%), aiding in argument mapping or identifying claims to verify.

The study emphasizes using models as an "editorial desk" with the student as editor-in-chief, especially for critical tasks like personal statements. Specific prompts can guide models to provide judgment without rewriting.

The current models tested include GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, reflecting the latest generations. This blind comparison method helps evaluate AI output on merit, not brand reputation.
